24 The siren of a moving police car emits a sound wave with a frequency of 440 Hz. A stationary
observer hears sound of frequency 494 Hz. The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s–1.
What could be the speed and the direction of movement of the car?
A
37 m s–1 directly towards the observer
B
37 m s–1 directly away from the observer
C
42 m s–1 directly towards the observer
D
42 m s–1 directly away from the observer

hints: Notice the observed $494\text{ Hz}$ is higher than the emitted $440\text{ Hz}$ - decide whether approaching or receding shortens the observed wavelength.
Recall the moving-source Doppler relation for a stationary observer: $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ when approaching with $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Rearrange to $v - v_s = v(f_s/f_o)$, substitute $440\text{ Hz}$, $494\text{ Hz}$ and $340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, then solve for $v_s$ and check $37$ versus $42\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: source frequency $f_s = 440\text{ Hz}$, observed frequency $f_o = 494\text{ Hz}$, wave speed $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, observer stationary.
State the rule: higher observed frequency means successive wavefronts are crowded together, so the car must be moving directly towards the observer.
Use the approaching-source Doppler equation $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$ where $v_s$ is the car speed.
Rearrange for the denominator: $v - v_s = v \times (f_s/f_o) = 340 \times (440/494)$.
Calculate with units: $v - v_s = 149600/494 \approx 303\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $v_s = 340 - 303 \approx 37\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Combine direction and speed: about $37\text{ m s}^{-1}$ directly towards the observer. This is option A.

A.explanation: Observed $494\text{ Hz} > 440\text{ Hz}$ means shorter wavelength, so source approaches, and $v_s \approx 37\text{ m s}^{-1}$ satisfies the Doppler equation.

B.explanation: Motion away from the observer would stretch the wavelength and give observed frequency below $440\text{ Hz}$, not $494\text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Towards is the correct direction but $42\text{ m s}^{-1}$ gives too large a frequency shift, about $503\text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: Motion away would lower the frequency, and $42\text{ m s}^{-1}$ would give about $392\text{ Hz}$, not $494\text{ Hz}$.
